root: ^Cornellius leans against a marble column, watching the crowd with an amused smirk. He notices you and raises his glass.

g-0: ^"Well, well. A fresh face actually exploring instead of clustering around the champagne fountain. How refreshing."
g-1: ^"Cornellius, at your service. Are you enjoying the spectacle?"

s: ^"You seem very knowledgeable about everyone here."
^"You seem very calm for such a tense evening."

knowledgeable_talk: ^He laughs. "That's what happens when you pay attention. Most people here are too busy performing to actually observe."

g-0: ^"Take Gaten, for instance—he's been checking Alistair's favorite sitting area every ten minutes like he's expecting a report card. The man can't function without approval."
g-1: ^"Brooklyn's the opposite—she's been holding court like she already wears the crown. Bold move for someone in her position. Then again, desperation makes people bold, doesn't it?"

unusual_talk: ^"Unusual? At a masquerade ball?" He grins. "Everything's unusual. But if you're asking if I've noticed the tension..."

g-0: ^"Derek nearly crushed a wine glass when someone mentioned military appointments. Flora's been avoiding Alistair's like he's the plague."
g-1: ^"And I could swear I saw Estelle crying near the discussion room’s entrance earlier. Poor thing looked terrified."
g-2: ^He shrugs. "But servants always have their dramas, don't they? Not really our concern."

calm_talk: ^"Why wouldn't I be calm? I've learned everything I know from the best. Alistair taught me that power is a game of chess, not checkers."

g-0: ^"You stay three moves ahead, you keep your mask on, and you never, ever let them see you sweat."
g-1: ^adjusts his silver cufflinks Alistair taught me everything... perhaps too well. A student eventually surpasses the teacher, don't you think?"
g-2: ^"Speaking of which, have you met dear Alistair yet? No? Well, he's probably in one of his 'discussions.' The man does love his private negotiations."

ending: ^Cornellius takes a long sip of his drink, his eyes scanning the room over the rim of his glass.
